questions.q: $A$ has shape $(3, 5)$. What shape must $x$ have for $A x$ to exist, and what shape is $y = A x$?
questions.explain: The number of columns of $A$ (5) must match the length of $x$; the output has one entry per row of $A$ (3).
Each output entry is a row of $A$ dotted with $x$: $1\cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 1 = 4$ and $3 \cdot 2 + (-1) \cdot 1 = 5$. Using the columns instead of the rows gives the wrong $(5, 1)$.

questions.q: How is the single output entry $y_i$ computed?
options: $y_i = \sum_j A[i, j]\, x[j]$ — row $i$ of $A$ dotted with $x$
$y_i = \sum_i A[i, j]\, x[i]$ — column $j$ dotted with $x$
questions.explain: Every output number is one row dot product: multiply row $i$ by $x$ entry by entry and add.

questions.q: What happens if $A$ is $3 \times 3$ but $x$ has 4 entries?
options: NumPy raises an error — the 4th entry of $x$ has no partner in a row of $A$
questions.explain: Each row of $A$ has 3 numbers, so a 4-entry $x$ cannot be paired up; the product $A x$ does not exist.
